title: Conveyance duty abolished on commercial property up to $1.5 million (ACT)
summary: From 6 June 2018 commercial property transfers of $1.5 million or less paid no conveyance duty, and a flat $5 per $100 applied above that, as part of the ACT's move from duties to rates.

commenced.what: Nil duty on commercial transfers up to $1.5 million

direction_rationale: Stamp duty on commercial and industrial property raises the cost of moving premises; abolishing or replacing it should make it cheaper for firms to relocate, expand and match to better sites.
comparison: Other states that kept commercial stamp duty
confounders: commercial property cycle and interest rates

verified.notes: Read on the ACT register (DI2018-116, notified 4 June 2018).

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: The ACT abolished conveyance duty on commercial property up to $1.5 million, moving to annual rates. Stamp duty is one of the most inefficient taxes: it discourages firms from moving to better premises and makes property slower to change hands.

marks.reason: Removes or replaces a transaction tax that Treasury estimates costs 72 cents of efficiency per extra dollar raised.
Lowers the up-front cost of buying business premises.

assessment.confidence_note: The efficiency case rests on Treasury's estimates of the cost of each tax; there is no ex post evaluation of these reforms here.
